sentences.text:
Heard on I.A.No.24624 of 2022, an application filed under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant Mukesh arising out of judgment dated 25/07/2019 delivered in Special Trial No.203/2017, by VI Additional & Sessions Judge, Chhindwara (MP).
The appellant has been convicted under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I.
for 10 years with fine of Rs.3,000/-, Section 323 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 1 year,
Section 313 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for Life with fine of Rs.3,000/-, Section 318 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.3,000/-, Section 342 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 1 year and Section 506 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I.
for 1 year, with default stipulations.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is urged that as per prosecution story, the complainant 'J' lodged a report in Police Station that in the year 2016 she used to visit Umreth for the purpose of learning stitching.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: During that period, she developed affinity with appellant who was running a cycle shop.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: A love affair developed between them.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: On 17/01/2017 when prosecution was going back to her village from stitching centre of Umreth, near Banjari Mata Temple, the appellant forcibly took her to the forest and sexually assaulted her.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: She did not narrate this incident to the family members.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text:
After one week therefrom,
the appellant again sexually assaulted her.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: He refused to solemnize marriage with the victim.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: The brother of appellant took her to his house and then appellant assaulted her.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: She was forcibly taken to Moredongri and with the help of a Nurse, the abortion had taken place.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: The brother of appellant and Nurse Nirmala were acquitted by the Court below.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Ms. Indu Pandey, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Court below has committed an error of law in convicting the appellant under Section 318 of IPC and imposing the sentence of 10 years R.I., whereas the maximum sentence prescribed under the statute for committing offence under Section 318 of the IPC is only 2 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Dr. D. Moitra (PW-11) is a Radiologist who deposed that he thoroughly examined the prosecutrix but did not find any symptoms of abortion.

sentences.text: The similar was the view of another Dr. Ranu Singh (PW-13).

sentences.text: The victim developed physical relations with consent.

Thereafter, from the date of judgment i.e.

sentences.text: The total sentence imposed is for a period of 10 years.

sentences.text: The appellant has already undergone half of the actual sentence.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: The case of prosecution is based on surmises and conjectures.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: The appellant has a fair hope of succeeding in the present appeal.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Thus, remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned Government Advocate opposed the prayer on the basis of objection.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: We have heard the parties at length and perused the record.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid factual backdrop, half of the sentence undergone by appellant, coupled with the fact that the final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Accordingly, I.A No.24624 of 2022 is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Mukesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2023.json

sentences.text: Subject to depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited), the remaining jail sentence of appellant Mukesh is hereby suspended and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court, Chhindwara on 08th May, 2023 and also on such other dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.

Ms. Sharmila Sharma - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Surendra Kumar Gupta, Ga for respondent/State.
Heard on I.A.No. 2026/2026 which is second application under Section 389(1)Cr.P.C./430 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of sole appellant - Mukesh.
opennyai_summary.final__facts:
The appellant has been convicted for the offence u/s 342 of IPC for a period of one year RI with a fine of Rs.500/-, u/s 376 (G) of IPC for a period of twenty years of RI with a fine amount of Rs.
2000/- and 506(2) of IPC for a period of one year with a fine amount of Rs 500/- along with a default clause.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
it expedient to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant.
The execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant - Mukesh shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal and he be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court and on depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 14.05.2026, and thereafter, on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during the pendency of the appeal.
